content.comment_body: Hello, If a 4-20 mA pressure transmitter outputs values between 452 and 480, and 452 represents 0.7M while 480 represents 2.75M in a water reservoir, I've set the analog amplifier parameters with gain at 7.32 and offset at -3238. These settings work but were found through time-consuming testing. Is there a simpler way to calculate gain and offset?
Hi [user_name], Could you specify what physical measuring range is associated with your 4-20 mA signal?

Typically, sensor documentation will state the sensor’s measurement range. You can enter these minimum and maximum values into an Analog Amplifier or corresponding scaling configuration. The gain and offset are then calculated automatically.
Hi. For reference: Min: 200 Max: 1000 Gain: 1 Offset: 0
No, I was asking for the actual measurement range of your pressure sensor. For example, is it 0-10 bar, or something else?
Here are the recommended settings for a 4-20 mA sensor with a measuring range of 0 - 6 bar.

Procedure to set up an analog amplifier: Consider how many decimal places should be shown on the display. For a 0-6 bar sensor, you can show 3 decimal places. 1. Select the appropriate sensor type (here, 4-20 mA). 2. Input the minimum value (here, 0). 3. Input the maximum value (here, 6000, with 3 decimal places). The software automatically calculates gain and offset. 4. Set the desired number of decimal places (here, 3).
